findings.title: Client removal event crashes when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
findings.body: The event listener now wraps cleanup in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` and calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent`. When the v2 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) is also enabled, `AdminPermissions.management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients()` now returns the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Because this runs inside a ProviderEventListener during client deletion, deleting any client in such a deployment will blow up with an UnsupportedOperationException (or leave the deletion inconsistent). The v2 path needs its own no-op/cleanup handling instead of routing through a method that always throws.

findings.title: Per-client resource lookup uses resource server id as owner while resources are created with client id as owner
findings.body: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` looks up the per-client resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, i.e. with owner = `server.getId()`. However `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates these resources with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`, i.e. owner = the client's id (`resourceServer.getClientId()`), which is a different value from the resource server's id. If the store filters by owner when a non-null owner is passed, the per-client resource created for a specific Clients permission will never be found here, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-clients resource and per-client grants/denies (e.g. a negative permission on one client) are ignored. Either pass `null`/the same owner used at creation time, or make creation and lookup consistent.

findings.title: Possible null resource dereferenced in findByResource for all-clients fallback
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can return `null` (it returns null when the resource store has no resource named 'Clients', e.g. for a resource server created before this schema type existed or after a failed init), so `findByResource(server, null)` will throw an NPE instead of simply denying permission. Add a null check on the returned resource before querying policies.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName()` only special-cases the Users resource type. For the newly added Clients type, per-client resources are stored with the client's UUID as the resource name (see `resolveClient` returning `client.getId()`), but the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is typically null for these programmatically created resources. Any UI/API that renders permission resource names (e.g. the admin console permission list) will show nothing or a raw UUID instead of the client's clientId. Add a Clients branch resolving the client and returning its clientId, mirroring the Users branch.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes return values for void methods
findings.body: The newly added Javadoc for `requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" and `requireViewClientScopes()` similarly says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException on failure. The documentation is copy-pasted from the boolean accessors and misstates the contract; it should say it throws ForbiddenException if the corresponding can* method returns false, as done for the other require* methods.
